differences: Both compute the same triangular matrix element; YIAN uses u64 indices and converts the bounded result to i32.
C receives double pointers and YIAN receives checked f64 slices; both sum products in the same increasing-index order.
C uses pointer parameters and YIAN uses f64 slices; both retain the serial i-then-j accumulation order.
C uses pointer parameters and YIAN uses f64 slices; both retain the serial i-then-j accumulation order and transposed A(j,i) access.
C reads the temporary array through global tmp; YIAN passes the same owned temporary slice explicitly.
C parses n from argv; YIAN compiles n through the bench-scale marker, with full/fast values 8000/1000.
C leaves its three malloc arrays allocated until process exit; YIAN owns and drops the three n-element slices after printing.
C uses printf with nine fractional digits; YIAN emits the same fixed nine digits through a dedicated formatter.
